title: Collaboration: Reject Stale Meeting Signaling After Reconnect
businessContext: A delayed disconnect from an old call ends a new meeting. Conflicting offers and early answers corrupt the signaling state.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ epoch, phase, offerId, events }). Initial phase is idle/offered/connected/closed; idle has null offerId, other phases have a nonempty offerId. Events have unique-or-replayed nonempty id, nonnegative safe-integer epoch, and type offer/answer/disconnect. Offer/answer have nonempty offerId. All shapes are valid. First deduplicate event IDs within this batch, consuming them even when rejected. Lower epoch => stale. Higher epoch accepts only an offer, replacing state with offered; other types => unexpected. At the current epoch: idle accepts an offer; offered/connected with same offerId => duplicate, different => conflict; closed rejects offers as unexpected. A matching answer changes offered to connected, or is duplicate if already connected; otherwise unexpected. Disconnect changes offered/connected to closed (preserve offerId), returns duplicate if already closed, and is unexpected while idle. Return { epoch, phase, offerId, outcomes }. No SDP, WebRTC negotiation, or media is executed.
constraints: Implement the synchronous solution(input) contract exactly. Do not mutate input; all inputs are JSON data.
This is a deterministic state model. It does not open sockets, send notifications, authorize real users, or establish media connections.
candidateTasks: Reproduce the starter failure, implement the invariant, and pass every authored case.
How would you add perfect negotiation, ICE restart, TURN fallback, and participant authorization to a real meeting service?
starterCode: function solution({epoch,phase,offerId,events}) { for(const e of events){epoch=e.epoch;offerId=e.offerId||offerId;phase=e.type==='disconnect'?'closed':'connected';} return {epoch,phase,offerId,outcomes:events.map(()=>'connected')}; }

testCases.name: Old disconnect cannot end a new call
Conflicting same-epoch offer preserves active offer
Early answer cannot create a connection
New epoch starts clean after disconnect
Wrong answer rejected and repeated matching answer is idempotent
Disconnect without an offer cannot create closed state

hints: Write down validation and replay precedence before changing state.
Use stable IDs and monotonic sequence/version values; preserve input ownership.
alternativeApproaches: Use an append-only event log with transactional projections.
Use a database snapshot plus a versioned resume cursor.
commonMistakes: Trusting delivery order or treating retries as new operations.
Mutating caller-owned arrays or accepting cross-channel data.
Presenting a fixture result as a guarantee of real-time delivery or media connectivity.
